# openobserve_pipeline_destination (Resource)

Manages an OpenObserve pipeline destination: an external endpoint a pipeline forwards records to through a `remote_stream` node.

This is the same underlying object as `openobserve_alert_destination`, stored through the same endpoints, and the server tells them apart by the `module` query parameter sent on create and update, which this resource always sets to `pipeline`. Without it the server stores an alert destination, and a pipeline cannot send to it. They are separate resources here because that choice decides what the object is for, and because the rest of the alert surface, templates, email recipients and SNS, does not apply to a pipeline.

Provider versions up to 1.4.2 did not send `module`, so a destination they created is an alert destination. The computed `module` attribute reads `alert` for one, and the next plan shows an in-place update that converts it. An alert that also sends to that destination stops working once it is converted, so point such alerts at an `openobserve_alert_destination` first.

The server refuses to delete a destination a pipeline still sends to. Referencing this resource's `name` from the pipeline's `remote_stream` node is what makes Terraform order the two correctly.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Where a pipeline forwards records. This is the same underlying object as an
# alert destination; the provider stores it as a pipeline one by sending
# module=pipeline on create and update.
# The server resolves the URL when the destination is saved, and rejects one it
# cannot reach with "Destination URL blocked by SSRF guard". The host has to
# exist by the time Terraform applies.
resource "openobserve_pipeline_destination" "warehouse" {
  name = "warehouse"
  url  = "https://example.com/ingest"

  # One JSON object per line. Leave unset to send one JSON array per request.
  output_format = "ndjson"

  headers = {
    Authorization = "Bearer ${var.warehouse_token}"
  }
}

# For a system OpenObserve knows how to format for, name it. Leave it unset for
# a plain webhook.
resource "openobserve_pipeline_destination" "splunk" {
  name             = "splunk_hec"
  url              = "https://example.com/services/collector"
  destination_type = "splunk"
  skip_tls_verify  = false

  metadata = {
    team = "platform"
  }
}

# Elasticsearch bulk format needs the index to write into.
resource "openobserve_pipeline_destination" "elasticsearch" {
  name                = "es_bulk"
  url                 = "https://example.com/_bulk"
  destination_type    = "elasticsearch"
  output_format       = "esbulk"
  output_format_index = "app-logs"
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Destination name, unique within the organization. Referenced by pipeline `remote_stream` nodes.
- `url` (String) Endpoint records are forwarded to.

### Optional

- `destination_type` (String) What is on the other end, when it is a system OpenObserve knows how to format for: `openobserve`, `splunk`, `elasticsearch`, or `custom`. Leave unset for a plain webhook.
- `headers` (Map of String) Extra HTTP headers sent with each request, for example an authorization header.
- `metadata` (Map of String) Free-form key/value pairs carried alongside the destination.
- `method` (String) HTTP method used to forward records.
- `org_id` (String) Organization the destination belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `org_id`.
- `output_format` (String) How records are encoded in each request: `json` (one JSON array), `ndjson` (one JSON object per line), `nestedevent` (one `{"event": ...}` object per line), `esbulk` (Elasticsearch bulk format, into the index named by `output_format_index`), or `stringseparated` (JSON objects joined by `output_format_separator`). Defaults to `json`, which is also what the server uses for a destination saved without one. Leaving it unset means `json`, not "whatever the server has": a destination whose format was set outside Terraform, for example `ndjson` in the UI, plans a change back to `json` on the first refresh after upgrading or on import. Set `output_format` to keep the format it has.
- `output_format_index` (String) Elasticsearch index the records are written to. Required when `output_format` is `esbulk`, and not allowed otherwise. OpenObserve also accepts an empty index, which sends each record with `"_index": ""`.
- `output_format_separator` (String) String placed between records. Required when `output_format` is `stringseparated`, and not allowed otherwise. An empty separator joins the records with nothing between them.
- `skip_tls_verify` (Boolean) Skip TLS certificate verification. Leave false outside development.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Resource ID in the format `{org_id}/{name}`.
- `module` (String) What the server stores this destination as: `pipeline`, or `alert` for one created by provider version 1.4.2 or earlier, which a pipeline cannot send to. When it reads `alert`, the plan shows an in-place update that converts the destination to a pipeline destination. The check runs only while state has no module recorded, which is after upgrading and on import, so it does not cost a listing of every destination on each refresh. Once state records `pipeline`, a destination re-saved as an alert destination outside Terraform is not detected again.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Pipeline destinations are imported as {org_id}/{name}.
terraform import openobserve_pipeline_destination.warehouse default/warehouse
```
